subject: Azure Marketplace: manifest audit, publish window & co-sell registration
messages:
From: Lucy Ho <lucy.ho@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: samir.patel@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Azure publish window + manifest schema gaps (AcmeCloud offer)

Hi Kimberly / Aditya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We started a quick pass on the publisher manifest and ran into two items that will block auto-publish in the portal:

- Plan -> PlanId mapping: our pricing CSV emits PlanId values that include a leading zero (e.g. 0012) which the portal normalizes to 12 and then fails the SKU tie.
- Offer identity claim: the tenant proof step is returning AM-identity-mismatch when we try to bind the publisher SP to the offer. We captured the portal trace and attached a screenshot.

Can you confirm the recommended approach? We can either: (A) re-emit PlanId as strings and update the manifest, or (B) ask Redwood to create a temporary alias mapping during publish.

Also, what is the next available publish window where we can do a monitored push? Our legal team needs the DocuSign link signed before we attempt the publish.

Attachments: acme_publisher_manifest_v3.json, sku_map_v2.csv, screenshots/portal-evidence-claim.png

Appreciate a quick sync — we’re hoping to avoid a second round of portal remediation.

—Lucy
Lucy Ho
Marketplace Program Manager, AcmeCloud Services

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lucy Ho <lucy.ho@acmecloud.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Azure publish window + manifest schema gaps (AcmeCloud offer)

Hi Lucy —

Thanks for the detail and the files; that helped. Quick answers up front:

- PlanId normalization: we can accept string PlanIds; the portal expects exact match between manifest and pricing CSV. The easiest path is for Acme to re-export PlanId as strings (preserve leading zeros) and attach the updated CSV. If you can’t, we can run a one-off mapping during publish but that adds a manual step and a slight publish-delay.

- Identity claim (AM-identity-mismatch): that looks like a service principal mismatch, usually caused by a different appId or spn than the one registered in the publisher account. I’ll start a validate flow from our side against your tenant binding and open a quick Azure support ticket if the SPA metadata still rejects it.

For the publish window: we have a monitored push slot on Friday 2026-11-27 14:00 PT (14:00-15:30 PT) where our ops team will be available for rollback. If that works for you, please sign the DocuSign by EOD Thursday so Legal can confirm.

I’ll loop Marissa for any SKU entitlement edge-cases and Aditya for the automation mapping option.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Partner Technical Lead, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Lucy Ho <lucy.ho@acmecloud.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Azure publish window + manifest schema gaps (AcmeCloud offer)

Looping in Vivek and adding a quick note on the mapping path.

If Acme chooses the alias mapping (option B), we can implement a lightweight PlanId normalization during the staging publish job: we add a transform that pads numeric plan ids to 4 digits before validation. That transform will be removed post-publish (our staging job keeps a trace). The caveat: any downstream co-sell identity matching must see the canonical PlanId, so we need to record the mapping in the offer metadata (I can add that field).

Marissa — please confirm there are no co-sell blocking checks if PlanIds are written as strings vs integers; I think co-sell metadata relies on Plan display names and Partner Center entitlement IDs, not numeric formatting, but we should be explicit.

Thanks,
Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Lucy Ho <lucy.ho@acmecloud.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Azure publish window + manifest schema gaps (AcmeCloud offer)

Quick confirmation from co-sell side:

- Co-sell registration will not fail solely because of a PlanId leading zero. The co-sell flow matches on Partner Center entitlement IDs and Publisher tenant claims. Still, keep the mapping documented in offer metadata so Marketplace and SalesOps have a single source of truth.

- Regarding the identity claim, if Azure returns AM-identity-mismatch we should capture the portal request id and include it in the support ticket. Kimberly — please push the portal trace to the Drive link and I’ll add the support bundle we hand to Azure.

Schedule: Friday 2026-11-27 14:00 PT works for me. Lucy — if you can confirm DocuSign is complete by 17:00 PT Thursday we’ll lock the slot and run through the staging checklist beforehand (manifest, sku smoke tests, entitlement checks).

—Marissa
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Lucy Ho <lucy.ho@acmecloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Azure publish window + manifest schema gaps (AcmeCloud offer)

Thanks everyone — DocuSign completed for the offer and the legal team greenlit the Friday monitored push. We updated the pricing CSV and re-exported PlanIds as strings (attached). Two small asks before Friday:

1) Can Redwood include the manifest->PlanId alias mapping in the offer metadata so our internal billing can reconcile?
2) If the Azure identity claim still fails during the binding step, can Redwood escalate the portal request to your Azure partner channel contact (we can provide the support ticket id)?

I’ve attached the updated files (acme_publisher_manifest_v3.json, sku_map_v2.csv). We’ll be on the 14:00 PT call and will have our infra lead Samir on standby.

—Lucy
Marketplace Program Manager, AcmeCloud Services
